hints.title: Start with the part of known sign
hints.body: For every real input, f(x)2≥0. An integral of this square over [0,3] is therefore nonnegative.
hints.recap: The square integral is the guaranteed nonnegative term.
hints.pitfall: The sign of f itself is not supplied.
hints.pause: In the given equation, which ordinary integral equals another ordinary integral plus a nonnegative quantity?

recall.reminder: An integral of a square is nonnegative; keep this separate from an ordinary signed integral.

hints.title: Cancel the common interval
hints.body: Write the integral from 0 to 3 as the sum over [0,1] and [1,3]. The common [0,1] contribution cancels in the given equation.
hints.recap: A definite integral can be split at an interior point and its two signed contributions added.
hints.pitfall: Do not infer that f is nonpositive everywhere merely from its integral.
hints.pause: Write an inequality for the integral over <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></math>.

recall.reminder: Add and subtract signed integrals over their actual intervals.

hints.title: Negate the existential claim
hints.body: Assume statement I fails. Translate that precisely into a statement about every value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow></math> on <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></math>, then consider the sign of its integral.
hints.recap: Negating a somewhere statement gives an everywhere statement with the property negated.
hints.pitfall: Preserve the equality boundary when negating an inequality.
hints.pause: Check compatibility with the integral inequality you derived and classify both claims.

recall.reminder: Negating a somewhere statement gives an everywhere statement with the property negated.

solution:
Let J=∫03f(x)2dx. Since a real square is nonnegative, J≥0. The given identity is

J+∫03f(x)dx=∫01f(x)dx.

Consequently ∫03f(x)dx≤∫01f(x)dx, proving II. Subtract the common integral on [0,1] to obtain ∫13f(x)dx=−J≤0.

If f(x)>0 throughout [1,3], this last integral would be positive, a contradiction. Thus f(x)≤0 for at least one x in [1,3], proving I. Both conclusions allow equality; f≡0 is an example.

Answer D: I and II.
knowledgePattern: Use nonnegativity of an integral of a square
